name: Tomato Chutney
subtitle: deep red cooked chutney, tangy and hot, for idli and dosa

ingredients.note: byadgi for colour, guntur for heat
skip it if the tomatoes are very sour
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Chop the tomatoes coarsely. They break down anyway.
Cool the fried mixture fully before grinding, or the chutney will froth and taste raw.
Keep 1 tbsp of the oil back for the final tempering.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp sesame oil and fry the urad dal and chana dal until golden, about 90 seconds.
Add the red chillies and fry 20 seconds until they darken and swell, then lift out the dals and chillies.
steps.tip: Removing them now stops the chillies burning while the tomatoes cook down.

steps.text: In the same oil, cook the onion and garlic until the onion is soft and edged with brown, about 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tamarind and salt and cook on medium heat for 10 minutes.
Keep going until the tomatoes lose all shape and the oil pools red at the sides of the pan.
steps.tip: Underdone tomato is the single reason this chutney tastes thin.

steps.text: Cool the mixture completely, then grind it with the reserved dals and chillies to a coarse paste, no water.
Heat the last 1 tbsp oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves and hing.
Pour the tempering over the chutney and stir it through.

storage: Keeps 5 days refrigerated in a clean jar. The sesame oil preserves it. Serve at room temperature; it also freezes for a month.
